_comment: Deployment contract shared by EVERY variant listed in onnx_variants below - there is deliberately one contract file, not one per network, because the variants agree on the observation layout, the action space, q_default, action_scale, the gains and the rate. That agreement is what lets the controller keep a single observation history and switch networks under it mid-stride, so splitting this into per-variant files would invite the two copies to drift apart and quietly break the hand-over. The controller checks each network's input and output widths against these numbers at load time. Trained with safe_rl/tasks/manager_based/velocity (Rl-Velocity-Aliengo). Joint order is the Isaac 'locosim_joint_names' order, which is identical to conf.robot_params['aliengo']['joint_names'].

notes.normalization: The empirical observation normalizer is baked into the ONNX graph (Sub/Div on 'obs'), so raw observations must be fed.
notes.imu_lin_acc: NOT the accelerometer reading. isaaclab.sensors.Imu reports (v(t) - v(t - control_dt)) / physics_dt + gravity_bias: the velocity difference spans a control step because the sensor buffer is lazy (update_period 0 and history_length 0 mean it is only recomputed when the observation manager reads .data, once per control step), while the divisor is the last dt handed to update(), which is the physics step. The dynamic part of the term is therefore scaled by control_dt / physics_dt = 20 ms / 5 ms = 4 and the gravity bias is not. Measured on the trained environment: dynamic ratio 3.99 and the identity above holds to 0.03 m/s^2. 'imu_lin_acc_model' above says so, and the deployment reconstructs the term from the accelerometer as 4 * mean(specific force over the policy step) + 3 * 9.81 * imu_projected_gravity - verified against ground truth in Gazebo at correlation 0.99 per axis. Feeding the raw accelerometer instead hands the actor's velocity estimator a signal four times too small, which is what made the deployed robot oscillate. THAT IS HISTORY, kept because it explains why this field exists: it was fixed at source in isaaclab.sensors.Imu (which now divides by the interval it actually differenced), and the networks in this directory were retrained against the fixed sensor. safe_rl.sensors.ImuCfg.finite_difference maps one-to-one onto the kinds here: physics_step -> 'specific_force', control_step -> 'mean_specific_force', upstream -> 'isaac_lazy_finite_difference'. These networks were trained with physics_step, hence 'specific_force' above: the accelerometer reading on the inference tick, fed through unmodified and not averaged. 'physics_dt' is unused by this kind and kept only as provenance - it is the training physics step, which is what the scale factor of the old kind was derived from. 'specific_force' is also what a contract with no imu_lin_acc_model at all is taken to mean, which keeps older contracts behaving as before.
notes.imu_projected_gravity: Unit gravity direction in base frame, b_R_w @ (0,0,-1); level base gives (0,0,-1).
notes.history: Each history block is oldest frame first, newest last, flattened as (history_length, width).
notes.actions: Raw (pre-scale) network outputs of the previous control steps; zeros before the first inference.
notes.onnx_variants: Actors sharing this exact observation/action contract, so the controller can switch between them without disturbing the history. 'normal' tracks the operator velocity command (Rl-Velocity-Aliengo); 'safe' is MEANT to come from UnitreeAliengoEnvSafeEnvCfg - the same env with the command range pinned to zero and far more aggressive reset poses, velocities and pushes, a stand-still recovery policy - but is CURRENTLY A BYTE-FOR-BYTE COPY OF 'normal', pending a retrain of that task against the fixed IMU. The safe stop therefore still holds station (measured: it settles), but it is the walking policy at zero command rather than a genuine fallback, so it shares the walking policy's failure modes instead of covering them. Check the two files differ before relying on the safe stop as a recovery. Feed 'safe' a zero command, which is the only one it ever saw.
